% Pattern: attach/announce. A sentence that announces the proof and goes on
% with a clause on what it proves, as "Here we prove Lemma~\ref{a}, which
% will allow us to infer ...", announces the proof after it. Seen in the
% gold pilot (set X).
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1.1
% want lemma-2 statement/lemma 1.2
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lemma-2
% want proof-2 proof - proves=lemma-1
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}[section]
\begin{document}
\section{One}

\begin{lemma}\label{l:one}
Every convergent sequence is bounded.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{l:two}
Every Cauchy sequence is bounded.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Take the ball of radius one around a far term.
\end{proof}

\section{The first lemma}

Here we prove Lemma~\ref{l:one}, which will allow us to infer that a
sequence with no bound has no limit $\lambda$.

\begin{proof}
Take the ball of radius one around the limit.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
